info.title: launchroom API
info.summary: Deploy, inspect and configure launchroom projects from scripts, CI and the launchroom CLI.
info.description: Bearer tokens from Settings → API tokens (or `launchroom login`). A token is bound to one team and acts as its owner there, narrowed to its abilities. Errors are `{"error": {"code", "message"}}`; lists are `{"data": [...], "meta": {"nextCursor"}}`.

get.summary: Request analytics of every project of the token's team
get.description:
Requests per project and hour (per day for `30d`) over all environments, totals against the previous period, the split by server and the top paths across projects.

Requires the `read` ability.

post.summary: Start a CLI sign-in
post.description: Open `verificationUrlComplete` in a browser, then poll `POST /cli/sessions/token` every `interval` seconds.

post.summary: Poll for the token of a CLI sign-in
post.description: `428 authorization_pending` until approved, `403 access_denied` when denied, `410 expired_token` when expired or already picked up. The token is returned once.

Git services deploy `sha`, else the head of branch `ref`, else the head of their tracked branch, with the environment's last deployed configuration (staged changes stay staged). `redeploy: true` deploys the current commit again.

Requires the `deploy` ability.

get.summary: Build and runtime log lines of an environment
get.description:
The log explorer's query: the newest lines of the range, oldest first. `meta.cursor` with `after` returns only newer lines.

Requires the `read` ability.

get.summary: Follow an environment's logs (server-sent events)
get.description:
Starts live runtime logs like the explorer's Live and renews them while the stream is open. Events: `lines` ({entries, cursor}), `reconnect`. Resume with `Last-Event-ID`.

Requires the `read` ability.

Request analytics of one service in an environment
get.description:
Requests per hour (per day for `30d`) by status class, totals against the previous period, the split by server and service, and the top paths (ids as `:id`, no query strings), referrer hosts and client classes. No addresses or user agents are stored.

post.summary: Deploy the latest version of a service
post.description:
Builds and deploys the latest commit of the branch the service tracks, or resolves an image service's tag again. Refused while the service is stopped or has staged changes (deploy those with `POST /environments/{environment}/deploy`). Databases, workers and crons restart instead.

Requires the `deploy` ability.

get.description:
Resolved like a deploy from the last deployed revision. With `secrets=1`, secrets are included when the token has `secrets:read` and the role may reveal them; otherwise their keys are in `withheld`. Audited.

Requires the `env:read` ability.

Requires the `deploy` ability.

post.summary: Stop a service

Its containers stop and its domains show a stopped page. Configuration, domains, volumes and deployments stay; unfinished deployments are cancelled. Applies at once, not as a staged change.

Requires the `deploy` ability.

AdvisoryDetailData.description: An advisory group's public record: plain text only (rendered as paragraphs and https links), references and the source.

AnalyticsAgentsData.description: Coarse client classes: browsers (a "Mozilla" user agent without a bot keyword), bots and crawlers, everything else.

AnalyticsData.description: Request analytics of an environment or one service. Status series are request counts per bucket, aligned with `timestamps` (bucket starts, UTC). `paths`, `referrers` and `agents` come from the edges' analytics windows; `pathRequests` is the traffic they cover, so the "other" row of the top routes is `pathRequests` minus the listed paths. `serversWithoutPaths` names edges that served traffic in the range but don't send paths yet (older servers).

AnalyticsPathData.description: One normalised path of the top routes: ids appear as `:id`, there is never a query string.

AnalyticsProjectData.description: One project of the team analytics overview: requests of all its environments over the range and per bucket, the previous period's requests, error shares, and its production environment for the drill-down link.

colorSlot.description: Slot 0–7 of the data palette (colour follows the project).

AnalyticsRange.description: Time ranges of the request analytics: the last 24 hours and 7 days in hourly buckets, the last 30 days in daily buckets (from the daily rollups).

AnalyticsReferrerData.description: A referrer host (never a full URL) and the requests it sent.

AnalyticsSplitData.description: One server or service of the analytics split: its requests over the range, error rate and requests per bucket.

removed.description: A server that was removed (revoked) since; its name may now belong to another server.

AnalyticsTeamPathData.description: One normalised path of one project, for the team overview's top paths.

AnalyticsTotalsData.description: Request counts over the range and the same length of time before it. Requests include 1xx (WebSocket upgrades), which are in no status class.

errorRatePct.description: 5xx share in percent; null without requests.

previousRequests.description: Requests of the previous period; null without any.

ApiAbility.description: What an API token may do. The single list: routes declare one (RequireTokenAbility) and self::grants() narrows the owner's role inside User::hasTeamPermission(), so a token never exceeds its owner and never reaches a permission no ability maps to (servers, members, team, exec, exposure; backups only through the opt-in `data:transfer` on the transfer endpoints). Values are stored on tokens: never rename one.

ApiTeamData.description: The team a token is bound to, with the owner's role in it.

ApiTokenClient.description: Where a token was created: Settings → API tokens, or a CLI sign-in.

ApiTokenData.description: A token as its owner sees it (never its secret): `GET /me`, Settings → API tokens.

CertStatus.description: A domain's certificate state as edges report it. Null on a domain: no edge has reported it yet.

ChangeEffect.description: What a staged change needs when deployed. Declared on Data properties with #[App\Data\Attributes\ChangeAffects].

ChangeItem.description: One staged change. `path` identifies the item for Discard (`services.svc_….deploy.startCommand`, `services.svc_….variables.var_…`). `before`/`after` are display strings and are never set for variables: a diff never carries values (not even ciphertexts).

ChunkReceiptData.description: The answer to an uploaded chunk.

CliSessionData.description: A started CLI sign-in. The device code is the CLI's secret for polling; the user code is what the person compares in the browser.

CliTokenData.description: The token of an approved CLI sign-in, handed out once.

ConfigCheckData.description: A launchroom.json checked against an environment: its problems and, for a dry run, the staged changes it would produce and what the trust rules would ignore. Never carries variable values.

ConfigContentInput.description: `POST /environments/{environment}/config/validate|diff`: a launchroom.json to check against the environment. Never stored.

content.description: The file's text, as it is in the repository (≤ 256 KiB).

ConfigExcerptLineData.description: One line of a launchroom.json excerpt around a problem.

path.description: Where the project reads the file from (the suggested file name).

content.description: The file, formatted (two-space indent, sorted keys, trailing newline).

revision.description: The deployed revision it was exported from; null = the current settings (staged changes included).

ConfigFileEnvironmentData.description: One environment on Settings → Config file: the last read of its launchroom.json.

ConfigFileProblemData.description: A problem in a launchroom.json: where it is (1-based line and column, the dotted settings path users see), what is wrong, what to do, and a few lines of the file around it. Excerpts never contain a value the check refused as secret-looking (it is masked before it is stored).

ConfigFileStatus.description: The outcome of the last read of an environment's launchroom.json.

CreateDeploymentInput.description: `POST /environments/{environment}/deployments`: a commit of a git service (`sha`, else the head of branch `ref`, else the head of the tracked branch), or `redeploy` of the current commit.

CreateVariableInput.description: Create a variable for the service (staged until deploy). Without `targets` it applies to the environment in the path only.

DataSubject.description: What an import or export reads or writes: a managed database or a service volume.

DeployEnvironmentInput.description: `POST /environments/{environment}/deploy`: apply the staged changes. `stage`: build and start, route only on Promote.

DeployEnvironmentResultData.description: `POST /environments/{environment}/deploy`: the new revision and the deployments it started (none when no service needed one).

DeploymentFailureClass.description: Why a deployment failed, shown prominently with hints.

DeploymentResource.description: A deployment of one service in one environment. `finished` is true once nothing more happens on its own: live (`active`), `failed`, `cancelled`, `superseded`, or `ready` (a staged deployment waiting for Promote).

DeploymentStatus.description: The deployment state machine. Every status change goes through Deployment::transitionTo(), which validates against this table and emits DeploymentStatusChanged. queued → building? → releasing? → rolling_out → health_checking → [ready →] routing → active any in-flight status → failed | cancelled; queued/building → superseded (a newer deployment of the same service instance collapses older ones); active → superseded (a newer deployment went live). `ready`: a staged deployment is healthy and waits for "Promote" to route traffic to it; the previous version keeps serving meanwhile. It can be cancelled (its workloads are removed). `planning` arrives with the build wave.

DomainKind.description: generated (platform wildcard, sslip.io or *.localhost), custom (user-owned, on-demand TLS) and per-deployment URLs.

DownloadLinkData.description: A one-use download link: valid for a few minutes, for the user who made it.

EnvironmentKind.description: Kinds of environments: exactly one production environment per project, any number of persistent ones, ephemeral previews per PR.

EnvironmentResource.description: An environment; `revision` is the last deployed revision number (null before the first deploy).

ExportRunData.description: An export as the UI, the API and the CLI see it.

sizeBytes.description: Bytes received so far while preparing, the file's size once ready.

ExportRunStatus.description: Lifecycle of an export: launchroomd uploads the file (`preparing`); a complete, checked file is `ready` to download until it expires.

ExportSource.description: What an export reads: the data as it is now, or a stored backup.

FindingCardData.description: One finding on the Security page: the service, the package and its fix, the advisory and its severity, the investigation line.

FindingCheckData.description: One evaluated rule (A1–A6) of a finding, as a checklist line.

FindingInvestigationData.description: The latest investigation of a finding, as a line on a card.

ImportResultData.description: What an import left behind (from the task's DataImportResult).

ImportRunData.description: An import as the UI, the API and the CLI see it. The source label never carries a user or password.

step.description: The live progress line of the running task.

safetySnapshot.description: Whether a safety snapshot was taken first.

transferId.description: The transfer the file came from (to try again without uploading).

waitingFor.description: While holding: the services it waits for, still running.

waitingOn.description: While holding: why they still run, when it's their server (offline, busy with an earlier change).

ImportRunStatus.description: Lifecycle of an import: a safety snapshot first when replacing, then the services that use the data are held, then the task imports. Before the task starts a run can still be cancelled.

ImportSourceKind.description: Where an import reads from (protocol ImportSourceKind).

InventoryComponentResource.description: One component of a service's live image.

InventoryPackageData.description: Search results grouped by package name.

InventoryUseData.description: One version of a package and where it runs.

InvestigationCheckData.description: "What we checked": one signal and its window.

state.description: `checked`, `partial` (couldn't check, e.g. a server offline) or `skipped`.

InvestigationLineData.description: One sentence of "What we found". `network` is the client network a firewall line is about; only owners and admins get it.

InvestigationReplicaData.description: One replica of an investigation in progress.

InvestigationReportData.description: An investigation's report: what was checked, what was found (sentences with a level), the next steps and the honesty line. Stored as `security_investigations.report`; no process commands, only program paths, and client networks only in `network` (owners/admins).

honesty.default: Someone who got in can remove their traces, so a clean result doesn’t prove nothing happened. The firewall only sees requests that match its rules, and launchroom keeps request details for 7 days.

InvestigationStepData.description: One of "What to do now", mapped to an existing action.

LogEntryData.description: One line in the project log explorer (direction.md §9.8). `id` is stable (chunk id + index), `level` is guessed from the text (error keywords, warnings, debug), `source` says whether it came from a build/release step or from a running service. Text is raw and rendered as text, never HTML.

deployment.description: Short SHA (or deployment id when there's no commit).

environment.description: Environment name, in project- and team-wide searches.

LogLineData.description: One log line of a deployment. `number` is stable for the deployment (anchors `#L42`); `section` is the timeline step it belongs to (plan, build, release, rollout, health, route, runtime); `step` the finer build step reported by the daemon (install, build, push, …). Text is raw and rendered as text, never as HTML.

MeData.description: `GET /api/v1/me`: the token, its owner and its team.

ProjectResource.description: A project with its environments (previews included).

PromotionClass.description: How a field behaves when promoting configuration between environments. Declared on Data properties with #[App\Data\Attributes\Promotion].

ResolvedEnvData.description: The resolved env of a service. `withheld` lists secret (or secret-tainted) keys left out because the token or the role may not read secrets, or `secrets=1` wasn't asked.

SecurityServiceRefData.description: Where something runs: a service in a project's environment, with the link to its panel.

logo.description: Logo key of the service (`nextjs`, `postgres`, …) or null.

ServerRole.description: What a server is used for. A server has a set of roles.

ServerStatus.description: Lifecycle of an enrolled server. pending_approval → online (approved) | revoked online ⇄ unreachable → offline → online revoked is terminal: the key is denied immediately.

ServiceActionInput.description: Body of `POST …/services/{service}/stop|start|restart` (D68). `processes`: an app's workers and crons stop, start or restart with it.

ServiceActionResultData.description: `POST …/services/{service}/stop|start|restart` (D68): the service after the action and the deployments it started (Start and Restart roll out a deployment per service; Stop starts none).

ServiceInventoryResource.description: The inventory of a service's live image.

ServiceResource.description: A service in one environment. `status`: `stopped` while it is stopped (D68), else the latest deployment's status while it runs, else `live` when a deployment serves, else the latest deployment's outcome, else `not_deployed`.

stoppedAt.description: When it was stopped (null: not stopped).

StartCliSessionInput.description: `POST /cli/sessions`: what the CLI says about itself; shown to the person approving (display only, never trusted).

StartExportInput.description: POST …/exports: the data as it is now, or a backup snapshot.

StartImportInput.description: POST …/imports: exactly one of transfer and sourceUrl.

TeamAnalyticsData.description: Request analytics of every project of a team: totals against the previous period, requests per project and bucket (aligned with `timestamps`), the split by server and the top paths across all projects (`pathRequests` is the traffic the path data covers).

TeamRole.description: Team membership roles and the role matrix. This is the only place that maps roles to permissions.

TransferData.description: A transfer as the UI, the API and the CLI see it. Never carries keys, digests of chunks or link tokens.

format.description: protocol DataFormat: postgres_custom, postgres_sql, mysql_sql, mongodb_archive, clickhouse_backup, redis_rdb, tar, zip

topFolder.description: The archive's single top folder, when it has one (volume imports).

TransferDirection.description: Which way a transfer's file travels: an upload (browser or CLI → dashboard → launchroomd) or a download (launchroomd → dashboard → browser or CLI).

TransferStatus.description: Lifecycle of a transfer: chunks arrive (`receiving`), the complete, checked file is `ready`; `failed` and `expired` files are deleted.

UpdateVariableInput.description: Change a variable in this environment only. Omitted fields stay.

VariableResource.description: A variable row that applies to the service in this environment. Secret values are never part of it.

VariableTargetData.description: One target of a variable: an environment (public id) or "all previews", optionally only for branches matching a glob.

VariableType.description: Variable types: config values are readable by anyone who can see the service; secrets are write-only after saving.

WafServiceCountData.description: A service in "Most targeted" or "Watching, not blocking yet".

settingsUrl.description: POST target of "Turn on blocking" (Log only services).

WafSummaryResource.description: `GET /api/v1/security/waf?range=`: firewall totals, per category and per service. No client networks.

code.description: unauthenticated, forbidden, missing_ability, not_found, method_not_allowed, conflict, validation_failed, rule_violation, idempotency_key_reused, idempotency_key_in_progress, rate_limited, server_error; CLI sign-in: authorization_pending, access_denied, expired_token.

ability.description: The ability the token is missing (missing_ability).

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

Unauthenticated.description: The token is missing, expired or revoked.

Forbidden.description: The token lacks the ability (missing_ability), or the owner's role doesn't allow it (forbidden).

NotFound.description: Not found, or it belongs to another team.

Invalid.description: Invalid input (validation_failed) or a refused operation (rule_violation).
